bull.b: Sustained sequential revenue growth, alongside operating capacity expected to reach about 206 MW, indicates improving commercialization of Soluna’s infrastructure. Continued deployment can broaden the revenue base and support greater operating leverage as newer sites move from construction into productive use.

A 6.3 GW pipeline gives Soluna a substantial long-term opportunity set in renewable-powered computing. Its focus on energy-intensive workloads and behind-the-meter renewable generation can differentiate the platform while supporting expansion into AI, HPC, hosting, and other higher-value compute markets.

Eliminating the major credit facility materially simplifies Soluna’s capital structure and releases liens on Dorothy project assets. Lower debt obligations should improve financial flexibility, reduce financing constraints around project development, and leave more asset value available to support the company’s AI and HPC expansion plans.

bear.b: Strong revenue growth has not yet translated into sustainable profitability. Very low gross margins and deeply negative operating and net results leave Soluna dependent on future scale, better site utilization, and improved economics. Until those changes occur, earnings remain vulnerable to operating and project-level cost increases.

bear.t: Substantial Cash Burn And Funding Dependence
bear.b: Negative operating cash flow and sharply negative free cash flow show that the current business is consuming capital rather than funding expansion internally. Continued development therefore depends on external financing, increasing exposure to issuance, financing costs, and capital availability while losses remain substantial.

The decline in proprietary mining revenue highlights the sensitivity of Soluna’s existing business to mining economics and the need to transition capacity successfully toward hosting and AI workloads. That pivot may improve diversification over time, but it also creates execution risk while legacy mining contribution is weakening.
